title: Secure Document Access Proxy
business: A legal firm managing sensitive client case files stored in a legacy document management system.
problem: Direct access to the legacy system is unauthenticated and resource-heavy, causing system instability when multiple associates query large document blobs simultaneously.
solution: Implementing a Proxy pattern introduces a stand-in object that intercepts requests to the legacy system, enforcing authentication checks and managing connection pooling before delegating the call to the real service.
steps: Define a common interface shared by both the real document service and the proxy object.
Implement the proxy class to hold a reference to the real service object.
Add logic within the proxy to validate user credentials before forwarding requests.
Incorporate lazy initialization or connection pooling within the proxy to manage resource consumption.
Replace direct client calls to the legacy service with calls to the proxy instance.
outcome: Improved system stability and centralized security enforcement without modifying the underlying legacy document management codebase.
limitation: The proxy introduces an additional layer of indirection, which can increase latency for every request. To check for this, monitor the time difference between the proxy receiving a request and the real service completing the operation.

questions.question: In Secure Document Access Proxy, what is the primary reason for using the proxy pattern?
options: To replace the legacy system entirely
To enforce authentication and manage resource-heavy requests
To increase the speed of the legacy system
To store all documents in a local cache
questions.explanation: The proxy acts as a gatekeeper to handle security and resource management before reaching the real service.
questions.evidence: Implementing a Proxy pattern introduces a stand-in object that intercepts requests to the legacy system, enforcing authentication checks and managing connection pooling before delegating the call to the real service.

questions.question: In Secure Document Access Proxy, what is a potential trade-off of this implementation?
options: Increased latency due to the extra layer of indirection
The legacy system becomes harder to maintain
The client must know the internal details of the legacy system
It prevents the use of connection pooling
questions.explanation: Adding a proxy layer adds a step in the execution path, which inherently introduces a small amount of latency.
questions.evidence: The proxy introduces an additional layer of indirection, which can increase latency for every request.
